newsitem.title: UK: Moody's says fiscal worries to top ratings agenda.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says fiscal worries to top ratings agenda.

text.p: Moody's Investor Service managing director David Levey said on Wednesday the rating agency would be keeping a close watch on the fiscal situation in a number of developed economies.
Levey said the fiscal issue was the main question for many European sovereign ratings, and that EMU (economic and monetary union) was only a small part of the equation.

"The main question for ratings will be whether governments can keep fiscal control with ageing populations and high unemployment," Levey told an IBC conference here on the impact of the euro on European securities markets.
"That is what we will be watching very closely."
Levey said some of the largest problems would be in France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Austria.
"Most European countries have problems but to varying degrees," he said, adding this partly depended on the average age of populations and the degree to which pension systems are funded.
Levey said fiscal problems would start building up fairly soon and projected budget deficits would be hit in five to 10-years time.
"This is where the centre of attention (for ratings) will be shifting to," he said.
